gen-dafont-azonix-gf-puritan: Authoritative and wide-mouthed, Azonix keeps its lines drawn with one fixed pen, crisp when shrunk. Puritan, with rounded forms and oversized e and a counters, stays approachable beside it.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-questrial: Questrial has a flat, stencil-cut feel and a tall band of letters. Beneath Azonix's commanding capitals, its single-weight strokes and open curves would keep paragraph after paragraph easy going.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-radio-canada: Tall, full lowercase under a commanding display face. Radio Canada keeps a steady line with a clear opening at each curve's end, while Azonix supplies wide-mouthed authority up top.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-radio-canada-big: Wide, commanding Azonix up top, then Radio Canada Big below with a monoline body whose x-height fills the line. Its terminals finish well away from the stem, so paragraphs keep moving smoothly.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-readex-pro: Authoritative up top, quietly professional below. Readex Pro, with broad terminal gaps and a steady weight from word to word, would carry long text smoothly beneath Azonix's wide-mouthed capitals.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-ruda: Azonix commands the top with crisp, wide-mouthed letters that survive shrinking. Ruda sits beneath with a wire-like monoline skeleton and a sizable x-height, softening the heading's firm stance on screen.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-saira: Saira reads clean, its s open enough to see through. What stands out is the gap between Azonix, whose strokes never swell or thin, and Saira's rounded letters stretching high toward the top line.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-sarpanch: Azonix draws round bowls whose outline never swells or thins. Azonix is best at commanding attention, while Sarpanch, a sans with a clearly open e and a compact ascender gap, is best at staying approachable.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-schibsted-grotesk: Tall-bowled e and a shapes keep the text approachable, never closing in at the terminals. Schibsted Grotesk carries that through paragraph after paragraph, under an Azonix heading with the weight of a drawn wire.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-sen: Sen builds its lowercase tall and traces each letter in a line of constant weight. Azonix is best at commanding attention up top, while Sen's curves stop short of turning inward.
